318669.literal_statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface with Euler characteristic $\chi$, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and let $G$ be a graph embeddable in $\Sigma$. Write $|V(G)|$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**General exact upper-bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ embeddable in $\Sigma$ has at most

$$
8|V(G)|-4(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})+2^{(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})/2}
$$

cliques, with equality if and only if $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$ and $G$ is obtained from $K_\omega$ by repeatedly splitting triangles.

The preceding bound $8(|V(G)|-\omega)+2^\omega$ is reported to fail for several surfaces without complete-graph triangulations, motivating this formulation in terms of the Euler characteristic. The conjecture gives the proposed exact extremal value for all surfaces.

319024.literal_statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let a **non-flowerable collection** be a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of $n$ coins from which no flower, that is, no coin graph representation of a wheel graph, can be formed. Let $NF(\mathcal{C})$ be the maximum number of edges of a coin graph formed from coins in $\mathcal{C}$), and define

$$
NF(n)=\max\{NF(\mathcal{C}):\mathcal{C}\text{ is a non-flowerable collection of }n\text{ coins}\}.
$$

Also let $E_4(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges of a plane graph on $n$ vertices in which every vertex bounds some $\ell$-gon with $\ell\geq4$.

**Non-flowerable extremal equality conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
NF(n)=E_4(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{11}{4}n-6\right\rfloor.
$$

The source proves only the upper bound $NF(n)\leq E_4(n)$ and explicitly says that equality is unknown at the time of writing.

328958.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a **Dirac graph**, meaning a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n/2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an **incompatibility system** over $G$, consisting for each vertex $v$ of a family of unordered pairs of distinct edges incident with $v$; edges in one of these pairs are incompatible. The system is **1-bounded** if every edge incident with any vertex is incompatible with at most one other edge at that vertex. A Hamilton cycle is compatible with $\mathcal{F}$ if every pair of its edges is compatible.

**Häggkvist's conjecture.** For every 1-bounded incompatibility system $\mathcal{F}$ over a Dirac graph $G$, there exists a Hamilton cycle compatible with $\mathcal{F}$.

The paper presents this as a conjecture of Häggkvist from 1988 motivating its study. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

335229.literal_statement:
A $2$-coloring assigns each vertex a red usage in $[0,1]$, with blue usage $1-r(v)$; the defect of a vertex is the sum, over its neighbors, of the overlap in their color usages, and $D(G,2)$ is the minimum possible maximum defect over all such colorings of $G$. **Outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture.** For any outerplanar graph $G$,

$$
D(G,2)<2.
$$

Ordinary $2$-colorings of outerplanar graphs have defect at most $2$, and the fan examples show that the minimum defect can approach $2$ from below. The conjecture asks whether the bound is always strictly improvable.

335547.literal_statement:
Let $B=(0;\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)$ be any non-trivial block decomposition of even weight $N$. **Alternate odd positions conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Alt}_{\{\ell_i\mid i\text{ odd}\}}I_{\mathrm{bl}}^{\mathfrak m}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)=0.
$$

The conjecture extends the analogous alternating identity for 123-multiple zeta values to arbitrary block lengths. It is proposed after the special case suggested by Borwein, Bradley and Broadhurst; no proof or disproof is given in the source.

336275.literal_statement:
Let $B$ be the butterfly poset on four elements $a,b,c,d$, with $a,b<_B c,d$. For a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, let $Tr_{n-1}(n,B)$ denote the maximum size of a family whose traces on all $(n-1)$-subsets contain no copy of $B$. **Butterfly trace conjecture.** If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
Tr_{n-1}(n,B)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the related exact formula $Tr(n,B)=\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+1$, but the asserted value for traces on $(n-1)$-subsets is posed as an open problem.

340053.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected balanced $S_{3,3}$-free bipartite graph, where $S_{3,3}$ denotes the corresponding forbidden subgraph. **Flandrin–Fouquet–Li conjecture.** There exists a constant $d$ such that if the minimum degree of $G$ is at least $d$, then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. This conjecture was proposed in 1994. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

341567.literal_statement:
Let $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ be the real coefficient sequence, and say that it **changes sign** at $N>0$ when $c_Nc_{N+1}<0$.

**Sign-change conjecture.** The sequence $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ changes sign infinitely often.

Numerical experiments find sign changes at $0,1,27,533,10457,\ldots$, but do not establish infinitude; the conjecture concerns the continuation of this observed oscillation.

343053.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition whose nonzero parts are distinct, and let $P_\lambda$ be its Schur $P$-function. **Schur-$P$ conjecture.** The normalized function

$$
\mathrm{N}(P_\lambda)
$$

is Lorentzian for every such partition $\lambda$. The source reports computational evidence for bounded largest part and number of parts; the assertion remains open.

343541.literal_statement:
Let $GP(n,3)$ be the generalized Petersen graph, with $n\geq 7$ odd, and let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote its minimum coprime number. **The $k=3$ minimum-coprime-number conjecture.** For every odd $n\geq 7$, 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(GP(n,3))=2n+3.
$$
 The source states that this has been verified for small values of $n$, while a minimum coprime labeling in the general case is not known there.

345564.literal_statement:
For integers $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, let

$$
\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]=\sum_r a_rq^r
$$

be the Gaussian binomial coefficient, so that $a_r=[q^r]\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The sequence of coefficients is **log-concave at $r$** when $a_r^2\geq a_{r-1}a_{r+1}$. **Central log-concavity conjecture.** For any fixed $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, the coefficient sequence is log-concave at every integer $r$ satisfying

$$
25<r<k(n-k)-25.
$$

Computations up to $n=430$ support this conjecture. It concerns the failure of global log-concavity for Gaussian binomial coefficients and predicts log-concavity throughout a broad central range, but no proof or disproof is given here.

345668.literal_statement:
For a distant pattern, write a square between two consecutive letters to indicate the constrained gap at that position. Consider the classical patterns $1234$, $1243$, and $2143$, and choose the same one of the three positions between consecutive letters in each pattern. **Square-placement Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** The resulting three distant patterns are Wilf-equivalent; for example,

$$
|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(1\square 234)|=|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(1\square 243)|=|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(2\square 143)|.
$$

The paper calls this conjecture surprising and notes that an analogous assertion for arbitrary Wilf-equivalent classical patterns is false, giving a counterexample in length four. It remains open in the stated special case.

346442.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d$ denote the Euclidean joint signature for a generic plane curve of degree $d$. The multiprojective witness-set dimensions are $\boldsymbol{e}_1=(1,1,1,1,0,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{e}_2=(0,1,1,1,1,0)$. **Euclidean joint-signature degree conjecture.** For $d\ge 3$,

$$
\deg \overline{\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d}=12d(d^3-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_1}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=8d^2(d^2-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_2}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=4d(d-1)(3d^2+d-1).
$$

These formulas were suggested by monodromy computations, which were successfully run for curves of degree up to $10$; their validity for all $d\geq 3$ remains open.

347079.literal_statement:
Let $n$, $k$, $d$, and $t$ be integers such that $n-1\geq d\geq k\geq 2$ and $d\leq t(d-k+1)$. Let

$$
\alpha=\binom{(t-1)(d-k+1)}{t-1}.
$$

The main theorem establishes that, when $\alpha\leq 3003$, there exists an $(n,k,d,\alpha)$-MSR code over some sufficiently large field. **Atrahasis-code conjecture.** The main theorem holds for all $\alpha$; equivalently, for every such choice of parameters, there exists an $(n,k,d,\alpha)$-MSR code over some sufficiently large field. The claimed extension is motivated by computations showing no counterexample for $\alpha\leq 3003$ and by the authors' belief that the determinant underlying both proofs is nonzero for all $\alpha$.

347689.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A graph has the **complete identity property** if every vertex can serve as the sink and the recurrent identity is the same configuration. If, for every vertex $v\in G$, attaching a single tree of size $1$ to $v$ results in a graph with the complete identity property, then

**Bipartiteness conjecture.** $G$ is bipartite.

The conjecture is motivated by a computer search showing that every connected graph with at most $10$ vertices having this property is bipartite, although not every bipartite graph has the property. Its general validity remains open.

350279.literal_statement:
Let $\sigma_{1,n}$ denote the largest singular value of the matrix associated with index $n$. **Largest-singular-value bound.**

$$
\sigma_{1,n} \leq \sqrt{2.0193n-0.7914}.
$$

This bound is suggested by the numerical homotopy experiment and is presented as a conjecture for the growth of the largest singular value.

351104.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected quartic graph, meaning a $4$-regular graph, and let its spectral gap be the difference between its two largest adjacency eigenvalues. For each $n\geq 11$, let ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ be the specified subfamily of ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}^*$: write $n-11=5q+r$ with $q$ a non-negative integer and $0\leq r\leq 4$, take $q$ middle blocks $M$, and choose the two end blocks according to $r$ as described in the construction.

**Abdi–Ghorbani's uniqueness conjecture.** For every $n\geq11$, the $n$-vertex graph of ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ is the unique graph with minimum spectral gap among connected quartic graphs of order $n$.

The preceding theorem shows only that every minimum-gap connected quartic graph belongs to ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}^*$; this conjecture specifies the unique member of the smaller family ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ that should attain the minimum.

352560.literal_statement:
Let $p_c(bb)$ denote the critical value for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane. **Small-intensity lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a $bb_0>0$ such that

$$
p_c(bb) > (\pi/3)\cdotbb
$$

for all $0<bb<bb_0$. The paper notes that the next-order expansion of $p_c(bb)$ could determine this inequality, although a different proof may also settle it.

354656.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $Delta(G)=4$ and **maximum average degree** $\operatorname{mad}(G)<4$. The **maximum-average-degree conjecture.** asserts

$$
\chi^2(G)\leq 13.
$$

Here $chi^2(G)$ is the 2-distance chromatic number. The bound would improve the currently noted upper bound of $15$; the source gives no resolution.

356915.literal_statement:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^3$ be a possibly singular K3 surface, and let $X_s$ be its smooth locus with curvature form $J$ induced by the Fubini–Study metric on $\mathbb{P}_\mathbb{C}^3$. Suppose that the singularities of $X$ are isolated and of type $A_1$. **Fubini–Study Chern number conjecture.** Then

$$
\int_{X\backslash \operatorname{Sing}X} c_2(J)-c_1(J)^2=24=\chi(\operatorname{K3}).
$$

The conjecture is prompted by numerical Monte Carlo evaluations for the family studied in the paper, where the displayed identity appears for the singular examples. Its general validity for all possibly singular K3 surfaces satisfying the stated hypotheses is not established here.

358626.literal_statement:
Let $\nu(r,k)$ be the largest $n$ such that every uniform oriented matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements has a $k$-neighborly reorientation. **McMullen's conjecture.** For every $r\geq 3$, 
$$
\nu(r,1)=2r-1.
$$
 This conjecture has been verified for $r\leq 5$ but remains open otherwise.

360524.literal_statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\delta^0(D)$ denote the minimum semidegree of an oriented graph $D$. **Stein's conjecture.** Every oriented graph with $\delta^0(D)>k/2$ contains every oriented path with $k$ edges. This would extend Jackson's result for directed paths to arbitrary orientations; it remains open.

365040.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an almost classical flat knot, and let $\bar J_\alpha(z)$ denote its normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial, defined using a minimal diagram of $\alpha$.

**Normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial conjecture.** For any almost classical flat knot $\alpha$, the normalized flat Jones–Krushkal polynomial satisfies

$$
\bar J_\alpha(-1)=1.
$$

This was observed empirically for every almost classical flat knot up to $10$ crossings. Whether the identity holds for all almost classical flat knots remains open.

365442.literal_statement:
An **equiangular tight frame (ETF)** is a matrix with unit-norm columns, constant-modulus pairwise inner products, and frame operator proportional to the identity. The conjecture concerns complex matrices with $d$ rows and $2d$ columns.

**Weak $d\times 2d$ conjecture.** For every $d$, there exists a $d\times 2d$ ETF.

This conjecture was posed by Fallon and Iverson and is the weakest of the paper's hierarchy of existence claims. The source reports substantial partial progress, including verification of the broader all-dimensional claim through $d=165$ and numerical evidence through $d=1500$, but the universal statement remains open.

366641.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\lambda_{n-1}$ and $\lambda_n$ denote its two smallest eigenvalues. **Strengthened eigenvalue conjecture.** One has

$$
\lambda_{n-1}+\lambda_n\geq -\frac{2n}{3}.
$$

This strengthens the original conjectured bound $c_3=\frac{1}{3}$ and was verified for all graphs of order at most $9$; the general case remains open.

371923.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}(D_k)$ be the Cartan matrix of the Dynkin diagram of type $D_k$, and let $f_{A,b,C}(q)$ denote the corresponding Nahm sum. **Zagier-duality conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, the Nahm sum

$$
f_{\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{C}(D_k),0,(1-k)/24}(q)
$$

is modular. This proposed identity is the dual counterpart of the modularity theorem proved in the paper for $f_{2\mathcal{C}(D_k)^{-1},0,-1/24}(q)$; its validity for all $k\geq 3$ remains open.

372553.literal_statement: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $4$, and consider the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$. **Divisibility conjecture.** The central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ is divisible by $4$ or $9$ for every $n>4$ except $n=64$ and $n=256$. This is the paper's starting problem; the abstract describes the corresponding assertion for $n>256$ as open, and the paper does not provide a definite answer.

372762.literal_statement:
For each fixed integer $d\geq 0$, define

$$
L(d):=\max\{n:p(n)\leq d+1\},
$$

and let $M_k(d)$ be the largest $n$ for which $p(n)$ is within $d$ of a $k$th power. **Merca–Ono–Tsai's stabilization conjecture.** There is a positive integer $N_d$ such that for all $k\geq N_d$,

$$
M_k(d)=L(d).
$$

The source attributes this to Merca–Ono–Tsai and gives no proof or resolution.

374733.literal_statement:
Let $C_{n,k}(q,p)$ be the $q,p$-Catalan triangle, and let $\mathfrak{S}'_{n,k}(312)$ denote the set of $312$-avoiding permutations represented in the triangle. For a permutation $\pi$, write $\operatorname{inv}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{coinv}(\pi)$ for its inversion and coinversion statistics.

**Bivariate combinatorial interpretation.** For all $n\ge1$ and $0\le k\le n$:

$$
C_{n,k}(q,p)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}'_{n,k}(312)}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}p^{\operatorname{coinv}(\pi)}.
$$

The identity has been verified for $n\le5$; the source attributes a proof to W5. Its status should be checked against that reference.

376077.literal_statement:
For integers $n$ and $c$, let $f(n,c)$ be the least integer $d$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a cycle with at least $c$ chords. **Kára and Král's conjecture.**

$$
f(31,31)=8.
$$

Their known bounds are $8\leq f(31,31)\leq9$, so the conjecture asks whether the lower bound is sharp. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.

376428.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a red/blue coloured $3$-graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_1(H)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. A **loose Hamilton cycle** is a cyclic ordering of the vertices in which every consecutive block of three vertices beginning at positions congruent to $1$ modulo $2$ forms an edge; it has $n/2$ edges. **The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles.** For every $\alpha>0$, there exist $\delta,n_0>0$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0$ and

$$
\delta_1(H)\geq \left(\frac{7}{16}+\alpha\right)\binom{n}{2},
$$

$H$ contains a loose Hamilton cycle with at least $(\frac{1}{4}+\delta)n$ edges of the same colour. This is proposed as the colour-biased analogue of the known asymptotically sharp minimum vertex-degree threshold $\frac{7}{16}\binom{n}{2}$ for loose Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs; the source gives no resolution.

379585.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph. Let $p(G)$ and $\widehat{p}(G)$ denote the minimum numbers of colors in a parity edge-coloring and a strong parity edge-coloring, respectively. **The bipartite equality conjecture.**

$$
p(G)=\widehat{p}(G).
$$

The paper gives examples with $\widehat{p}(G)>p(G)$, but all such examples contain odd cycles; whether equality holds for every bipartite graph remains open.

384074.literal_statement:
(Macri) Construct Bridgeland stability conditions on degenerate
 varieties, for example, the hypersurfaces with equations $x_0x_1\dots x_n=0$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$, especially for $n =2,3,4$. Given $[C]\in\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ arbitrary, is there a 
 description of the space of stability conditions on $C$? This is known some some irreducible nodal curves.

 (Schmidt) Are there Bogomolov type inequalities
 for stable objects on degenerate varieties?

384627.literal_statement:
Consider the following problems:
	\begin{enumerate}
 \item Find the best $C>0$ such that for all $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \mathbb{R}$, 
 

$$
\|f\|_2\le C^{\deg(f)}\|f\|_1.
$$

 \item For $1< p < q \le 2$, find the best $C_{p,q}>0$ such that
 

$$
\|f\|_q\le C_{p,q}^{\deg(f)}\|f\|_p.
$$

 \item How about the $d$-homogeneous analogs of the above two problems? Of particular interest, find the best $C>0$ such that for all $2$-homogeneous polynomial $f(x)=\sum_{i < j}a_{ij}x_i x_j$ over $\{-1,1\}^n$ for all $n\ge 1$, we have 
 

$$
\|f\|_2\le C\|f\|_1.
$$

	\end{enumerate}

384688.literal_statement:
For $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and unit vectors $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\in \ell_2$, consider the following two properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(a)] $\langle v_i, v_j\rangle \le 2\varepsilon$ whenever $i\neq j$, and
 \item[(b)] for each $i$, there exists $A_i\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|A_i|\ge n^{1-\delta}$ and
 $\langle v_i, v_j\rangle \ge \varepsilon$ for all $j\in A_i$.
\end{enumerate}
What is the largest $\delta$, in terms of $\varepsilon$, such that for any unit vectors
$v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\in \ell_2$ satisfying (a) and (b), there exists $I\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with

$$
|I|\ge n^{1-O(\delta)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{1}{|I|^2}\sum_{i,j\in I}\langle v_i, v_j\rangle = \Omega(\varepsilon)\, ?
$$

384823.literal_statement: Let $x_0$ be a uniformly random unit vector and observe $Y = \lambda x_0^{\otimes d} + W$ where $W$ is a symmetric tensor with $W_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ independently (up to symmetry). Let $\lambda^\mathrm{Bayes}$ and $\lambda^\mathrm{ML}$ denote the thresholds at which Bayes-optimal inference and maximum-likelihood estimation (respectively) achieve non-trivial correlation with the truth $x_0$. It is conjectured that $\lambda^\mathrm{Bayes} = \lambda^\mathrm{ML}$. These thresholds are also conjectured to be equal for the case $d = 2$ when $x_0$ has entries sampled i.i.d.\ from $\mathrm{Unif}\{\pm 1/\sqrt{n}\}$.

386187.literal_statement:
Compute multi-point (spatial) distribution for KPZ with various initial data. For example, with $\mathcal{Z}_0(x)=\delta_{x=0}$, let

$$
\mathcal{Z}(t,x)=e^{-\frac{x^2}{2t}+t^{1/3}A_t(t^{-2/3}x)-\frac{t}{24}}.
$$

What is the distribution $F(\xi_1, \xi_2)$ such that

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(A_t(x_1)\leq\xi_1, A_t(x_2)\leq\xi_2\right)=F(\xi_1,\xi_2)?
$$

Perhaps easier, show that as $t$ goes to infinity and space is scaled like $t^{2/3}x$, the process $A_{t}(t^{2/3}x)$ converges to the Airy$_2$ process in $x$.

390303.literal_statement: Fix a basis for Fn and let An−1⊂ Aut(Fn) be the copy of Aut(Fn−1) corre- sponding to the first n− 1 basis elements. Let φ:Aut(Fn)→G be a homomorphism of groups. If φ(An−1) is finite, must the image of φ be finite? Note that the obvious analog of this question for GL( n, Z) has a positive answer and plays a role in the foundations of algebraic K-theory. A diﬀerent approach to establishing Property (T) was developed by Zuk [ 85]. He established a combinatorial criterion on the links of vertices in a simply connected G-complex which, if satisfied, implies that G has property (T): one must show that the smallest positive eigenvalue of the discrete Laplacian on links is suﬃciently large. One might hope to apply this criterion to one of the natural complexes on which Aut( Fn) and Out( Fn) act, such as the spine of Outer space. But David Fisher has pointed out to us that the results of Izeki and Natayani [ 55] (alternatively, Schoen and Wang – unpublished) imply that such a strategy cannot succeed.

390377.literal_statement: Yet another idea is to go back to a decription of cobordism I once heard. I think this description is in print somewhere, but I don't know where or who wrote it. I believe this idea is a geometric description of MU^* X. Think of X as a simplicial set. Over each vertex of X put a manifold. Over each edge of X put a bordism between the manifolds at the vertices. Over each triangle, put a bordism between the bordisms on the edges--I don't really know what these means, but orientation must be involved. Continue in this way, and that is an element of MU^* X. There must be some equivalence relation you put on these, but I don't know what it is. The problem would then be to figure out whether this works and if it has been published, then to determine how you get K-cohomology from this description--presumably the bordisms between bordisms go away, so are the identity, and this is the cocycle condition for vector bundles. Then figure out how to get elliptic cohomology.

392850.literal_statement: For every fixed $\\varepsilon>0$, the $\\varepsilon$-dense Group Steiner Tree Problem on unweighted graphs admits a polynomial-time approximation scheme. Here an instance consists of a graph $G=(V,E)$ with pairwise disjoint groups $S_1,\\ldots,S_m\\subseteq V$, and the objective is to find a minimum-edge tree containing at least one vertex from each group. Writing $S=\\bigcup_i S_i$, the instance is $\\varepsilon$-dense when $|N_{V\\setminus S}(S_i)|\\geq \\varepsilon |V\\setminus S|$ for every $i$.
